what_its_for: Eltrombopag is used to increase platelet counts in your blood. Platelets are tiny cells that help your blood clot when you have a cut or injury. This medicine is used when your platelet count is too low, which can happen with a condition called immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), or with certain types of low blood counts caused by hepatitis C treatment or some bone marrow disorders like aplastic anemia.
how_to_take: Take eltrombopag by mouth once daily, on an empty stomach — at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after eating. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the tablets. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. If you take antacids, dairy products, calcium-rich foods, or supplements containing calcium, iron, magnesium, aluminum, selenium, or zinc, wait at least 4 hours before or after taking this medicine, as these can block your body from absorbing eltrombopag properly.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition, your platelet count results, and how your body responds to the medicine. The typical starting dose for adults with ITP is 50 mg once daily, but your dose may be adjusted up or down. Some patients, such as those of East Asian descent or those with liver problems, may start at a lower dose of 25 mg per day. Do not change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store eltrombopag tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container and away from moisture and heat. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids, vitamins, or mineral supplements (especially those containing calcium, iron, magnesium, aluminum, selenium, or zinc) within 4 hours of taking eltrombopag. Avoid dairy products such as milk, yogurt, and cheese close to the time you take your dose. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice unless your doctor says it is okay. Avoid driving or using machinery if you feel dizzy. Do not take any new medicines, herbal products, or supplements without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe stomach pain, unusual swelling or pain in your legs, sudden chest pain or difficulty breathing, sudden severe headache or vision changes, confusion, or any signs of bleeding such as blood in your urine or stools, unusual bruising, or bleeding that will not stop. Also contact your doctor if you develop any new eye problems, since this medicine can rarely affect your vision. Tell your doctor about any signs of infection such as fever or chills.
when_it_works: Eltrombopag usually begins to raise your platelet count within 1 to 2 weeks of starting treatment. Your doctor will regularly check your blood counts to see how the medicine is working and to adjust your dose if needed. It is important to keep all of your scheduled blood test appointments. The medicine helps manage your condition but may not cure it — do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): Use with caution as older patients may be more sensitive to side effects. Children: This medicine may be used in children aged 1 year and older with ITP; the dose will be calculated by the doctor based on age and weight. Pregnancy: Eltrombopag may harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Effective birth control should be used during treatment. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Liver disease: If you have liver problems, your doctor will start you on a lower dose and monitor you more closely. East Asian patients (including Chinese, Japanese, Korean, or Taiwanese): You may need a lower starting dose because your body may process this medicine differently.
